stories.title: What the Air Looks Like
stories.blurb: Everything else on this site is a number. Thirty-one photographs are not, and it is worth saying why they are here.

stories.title: How to Read the JanVayu Map
stories.blurb: The map now holds a number for every place in India. Not every city — every place: all 983,149 administrative areas the country is divided into, from the 36 states down to the 584,615 villages, and every gram panchayat, block, district,…

stories.title: Why We Lead With PM2.5, Not AQI
stories.blurb: At a conference last week, a reader made a point worth acting on: our headline figures often led with AQI, when PM2.5 is the measure that carries the health consequences.

stories.title: We Were Measuring the Wrong Green
stories.blurb: Earlier today we published a result that bothered us. We had put surface temperature on all 70,417 of India's municipal wards, and green cover alongside it, and the two barely moved together: a national correlation of −0.07.

stories.title: Surface Heat on Every Ward in India — and What It Showed
stories.blurb: The map has a new Colour menu. Alongside annual air, you can now shade any boundary by surface heat, and — for wards — by green cover and built-up share.

stories.title: One Map, Every Boundary in India
stories.blurb: Until yesterday, finding out how polluted your neighbourhood is meant knowing something you shouldn't have to know: whether the place you live is officially a ward or a village.

stories.title: Agartala Breathes Like the Coal Belt, and Nobody Was Looking
stories.blurb: India's Northeast is usually described in one breath: hills, forest, clean air. For most of the region that is simply true.

stories.title: Every Capital, and the Directory We Never Read
stories.blurb: This morning we published a post saying West Bengal's municipal wards were not openly available.

stories.title: Ninety Cities, Ward by Ward — and the One We Had to Go Somewhere Else For
stories.blurb: If you live in an Indian city, the number you see on the news is a city average. It is one figure standing in for a few million people, and it hides the thing you actually want to know: whether your neighbourhood breathes worse than the…

stories.title: Every Village in India Is Now on the Map — Including the Ones No One Measures
stories.blurb: India's air pollution story is told almost entirely through its cities. Delhi in November.

stories.title: The Air Your MP Answers For: Our Maps Now Cover 39 Cities, 543 Constituencies, and the Places the Smoke Starts
stories.blurb: Until this week, our ward map could show you fifteen cities. If you lived in Patna, Ludhiana, Ghaziabad or Indore — some of the most polluted places in the country — the answer to "how bad is my ward?" was: we don't have the boundaries.

stories.title: Testing the Chatbot to Make It Reliable
stories.blurb: These days we ask chatbots almost everything. Sometimes we ask them things that really matter — like whether the air outside is safe to breathe.

stories.title: You Don't Need to Code to Make India's Air Data Better
stories.blurb: People assume there are only two ways to help a project like JanVayu: write code, or send money.

stories.title: Why JanVayu's Mascot Is a Sparrow
stories.blurb: Meet Vayu Gauraiya — vayu, the air; gauraiya, the house sparrow. She's the face of Ask JanVayu, our chatbot — the little watchful friend who greets you when you come with a question.

stories.title: The Robots That Keep JanVayu Honest: How Routines Maintain the Platform
stories.blurb: A platform that holds others accountable with numbers has no business letting its own numbers rot.

stories.title: We Fact-Checked Our Own Site — and Changed 33 Numbers
stories.blurb: JanVayu exists to hold others accountable with numbers. So the numbers had better be right.

stories.title: A Working Language Switcher, an Accessibility Sweep, and a Much Lighter Site
stories.blurb: This week's releases (v26.6.58 to v26.6.71) were less about new panels and more about the plumbing: making what already exists work properly, load faster, and reach more people.

stories.title: What Shipped This Week: Forecasts, Fire Maps, and Pollution Beyond the Lungs
stories.blurb: We shipped five releases over the past few days (v26.6.43 to v26.6.47). Here is what changed and why it is useful.

stories.title: The Pollution You Can't See Being Emitted: Up to 42% of India's PM2.5 Is Made in the Sky
stories.blurb: When we picture air pollution, we picture a source: a truck's exhaust, a brick kiln's chimney, a field of burning stubble, a cloud of construction dust.

stories.title: The Citation That Didn't Exist: How We Found "Krishna et al." Was Really Jaganathan
stories.blurb: An accountability platform lives or dies by its citations. If we ask the public to trust a number — 1.72 million deaths a year, a +10 µg/m³ rise causing 8.6% more all-cause mortality — we owe them a source they can open, read, and check.

stories.title: Ask JanVayu Can Now Answer About Your Ward
stories.blurb: When we built the Ward Atlas — a map of every municipal ward across 14 cities, coloured by air, heat, green cover and built-up area — it lived only on the map.

stories.title: Live vs Annual: The Honest Version of "How Polluted Is Your Ward?"
stories.blurb: When we built the Ward Atlas — a map that colours every municipal ward of a city by its air, heat, green cover and built-up area — we ran into a question that's easy to get wrong, and that a lot of dashboards do get wrong.

stories.title: A City Is Not One Number: Mapping India's Air Ward by Ward
stories.blurb: When the news says "Delhi AQI is 320," it hides something important: there is no single Delhi.

stories.title: The Same Sun, a Different City: Why Your Neighbourhood's Heat Is an Air-Quality Story
stories.blurb: On a peak summer afternoon, a CSE satellite thermal survey of Delhi recorded land-surface temperatures reaching nearly 61°C in its most built-up, treeless zones while tree-covered areas like Lutyens' Delhi and the Yamuna floodplain…

stories.title: Quality You Can Measure: Lighthouse, axe, Lazy-Loading, Mobile
stories.blurb: The same day we shipped six Learning Games and refreshed the May 2026 data, we did a quieter but arguably more important thing: we made the platform's quality measurable on every PR.

stories.title: Six Learning Games: Jeopardy, Quiz, Source Matcher, Snakes & Ladders, Jodi Match, Tambola
stories.blurb: We have shipped a self-paced Learning Games panel — six short games, all original, designed for classrooms, RWA meetings, family movie nights, and idle ten-minute browsing on a phone.

stories.title: Data Refresh, May 2026: Latest Numbers, Updated Hero
stories.blurb: We try to publish the source-of-truth dataset for India's air quality crisis. That only works if we keep the front-of-site numbers current.

stories.title: What's New: Cigarette Equivalence, City Rankings, Community Sensors, Workshops
stories.blurb: JanVayu shipped its largest single update since launch this week. Here is what changed, why, and what each piece is for.

stories.title: IQAir 2025: India's Air Got Worse
stories.blurb: On March 24, 2026, IQAir released its eighth annual World Air Quality Report — the most comprehensive global assessment of PM2.5 pollution, covering 9,446 cities across 143 countries.

stories.title: The Lancet's Causal Evidence: 1.5 Million Deaths (Jaganathan et al. 2024)
stories.blurb: For years, the relationship between air pollution and death in India has been described in the language of association.

stories.title: NCAP at the Finish Line: Has India's Clean Air Programme Worked?
stories.blurb: In January 2019, India launched the National Clean Air Programme with a promise: reduce particulate matter concentrations by 20 to 30 percent across 131 cities by 2024, later revised to 40 percent by 2025-26.

stories.title: India's Children Are Paying the Price
stories.blurb: Air pollution in India is not an abstract environmental problem. It is a child health emergency.

stories.title: How Farmers Outsmart Satellites: The Stubble Burning Shell Game
stories.blurb: Every October, as the kharif paddy harvest ends across Punjab and Haryana, a familiar ritual begins.

stories.title: The $339 Billion Question: What Pollution Costs India
stories.blurb: India's air pollution crisis is usually framed as a health emergency. It is that.
